future_design_obligations: Keep all legacy-prefixed Sass and component HTML/CSS/SCSS byte-identical; preserve existing module namespace bindings, historical Sass API forms and selectors.

Map all historically configurable color roles, primary/accent/warn/unthemed and disabled states, ripple/focus/hover/pressed semantics, typography and density; avoid a repair limited to the two witness token names.

Use independently owned Material16 values. Current m2/private sources may explain behavior as evidence, but product code may call only the stable public root checkbox-overrides/button-overrides APIs present on both pinned floors.

Enumerate each supported public token and consumer path on both floors. Checkbox historical unselected-pressed-icon-color has no corresponding current public override token: prove the current pressed-state consumer before deciding whether an override is required; never blindly forward the entire historical map.
Preserve default/positive/negative density behavior and current public token clamps while retaining the historical source-call contract. Do not change legacy geometry or ask consumers to edit styles.
Preserve arbitrary foreground/background maps, CSS-variable palettes/contrast fallback, typography strings and scoped theme invocation.

Define exact full CSS differences with genuine untouched16 expected inputs for source-call semantics, current component proof for bridge output, and independent expected current values; never produce expected values from candidate CSS.

Do not silently broaden the existing finite two-module spinner/snack source subject. Any additional changed product closure needs a separate exact before/after source subject and explicit composed current-source proof, followed by narrow existing tool/report integration.

Keep the four earlier compiler observations immutable. New product-validation compile budget requires a concrete bounded matrix; avoid full builds/matrices and use Actions after implementation is plausibly complete.
Protect immutable goldens/catalogs/rosters/security review/canonical SHA disposition counts. This design grants no audit admission, G11, packed or rendered pass.
